features.title: OSPF DR/BDR Election
features.topology: R1–R4 share 10.0.123.0/24 through SW1. Each Gi0/1 is 10.0.123.<router number>, broadcast, cost 10. Router IDs 1.1.1.1 through 4.4.4.4. Priorities 100/50/0/0 elect R1 DR and R2 BDR; R3/R4 remain DROTHER. PC1 is 192.168.30.10/24 behind R3 Gi0/0 192.168.30.1; PC2 is 192.168.40.10/24 behind R4 Gi0/0 192.168.40.1.
checks: election practice is an independent seven-node shared segment with no OSPF/static routes or completion credit
published IOS configurations and completed reference earn eight live goals and require two real echo checks for ten tasks
four router LSAs and actual OSPF exchanges produce ten Full directed peers and two normal DROTHER 2WAY relationships
DROTHER LANs stay passive and advertise their prefixes without sending Hellos toward either PC
raising BDR or DROTHER priority does not preempt an established DR, and planned-priority goals remain live
DR failure promotes the BDR, keeps DROTHER LAN traffic working and makes the returning higher-priority router BDR

loss of both eligible routers leaves priority-zero DROTHERs 2WAY without remote routes until a DR returns

a later higher-priority R1 does not displace R2 configured first, and the controlled shared-segment reset restores intended roles

verificationNotes: Both original practice labs start with addressed interfaces, reachable host gateways and no router static routes or OSPF process. Their completion score is zero. All published commands execute through IOSSession; no neighbor, route, LSA or echo observations are fabricated.

Point-to-point: interface-based OSPFv2 Area 0, passive LANs, active point-to-point Ethernet transit and explicit cost 10. Received Hello/database packets produce FULL/- peers with no DR/BDR or transit Network LSA. Remote /24 routes require O, AD 110, metric 11, correct next hop and outgoing interface. Two real echo tests follow six live goals.

Point-to-point negative cases cover transit shutdown and recovery, received Dead-timer expiry on a physically up lossy link, passive transit, area/timer mismatch, withdrawn LAN membership and wrong cost. Local gateways stay reachable during transit failure; no alternate path exists.

Priority-zero point-to-point peers still form Full. Both priority-zero broadcast peers remain 2WAY/DROTHER without remote routes or replies. Normal-priority broadcast can carry traffic but cannot earn point-to-point network-type credit. Different local process IDs can interoperate but do not earn the planned process-10 goal.

DR/BDR: four broadcast routers, with client LANs behind the two DROTHERs. Ten directed Full relationships and two normal 2WAY/DROTHER relationships are checked against exact peers/interfaces. Each router receives all four router LSAs; the shared Network LSA is originated by the DR and lists all four attached routers.

DR/BDR priorities 100/50/0/0 and observed interface roles are separate live requirements. Raising BDR priority to 200 or DROTHER priority to 255 does not preempt the incumbent DR. A newly eligible or returning higher-priority router also does not preempt. Fresh equal-priority and default-priority saved-lab elections use router-ID tie breaking.

DR failure promotes BDR; with both remaining DROTHERs at priority zero, there is no eligible replacement BDR. Actual PC traffic continues after convergence. Returning R1 becomes BDR while R2 remains DR; a controlled shared-segment shutdown and R1-first restart restores intended roles.

If both eligible routers disappear, the priority-zero DROTHERs stay 2WAY. Received Dead-timer expiry is allowed before asserting withdrawal of retained remote routes. Local gateways remain reachable, and restoring an eligible DR recovers routing.

DR/BDR negative cases include passive transit, one-sided area mismatch, withdrawn LAN advertisement, wrong cost, incorrect priority/roles and a different startup order. Successful traffic cannot substitute for the intended election or route metrics.

DROTHER-to-DROTHER data forwarding uses the installed next hop across the shared switch and bypasses DR/BDR. Packet-event assertions and bidirectional traceroute verify that the DR is not a mandatory data-plane next hop.

Fixed IOS OSPF membership removal: no ip ospf <process> area <area> removes membership bindings while retaining independent network type, cost, timers, priority and authentication. An empty feature object is cleaned up. Area-change recovery and portable persistence regressions verify the repair.

Bounded optional configuredPriority and role fields extend the existing OSPF-interface lesson predicate. Priority is 0–255 and role is a known enum. Legacy OSPFv2 and OSPFv3 criteria still work; malformed imported values are rejected.

Both completed references earn only configuration/operational goals after real convergence. Two genuine traffic tests finish each guide. Saved reload, failure-state reload and individual startup reboot reconstruct protocol state; fresh traffic verifies current forwarding.

Each new lab passed six offline file:// browser scenarios: light/dark at 1440, 390 and 320 pixels, sequentially in isolated persistent Chrome profiles. Point-to-point cases include broadcast/priority-zero comparison and transit-failure reload/recovery. Election cases include non-preemption, BDR promotion, live traffic during DR failure, failed-DR reload, returning R1 as BDR, and controlled shared-segment recovery.

Four permalink cases preserve the current host/path/query without replacing an open workspace. Seven generic catalog regression checks pass, including accurate ten-lab Routing counts, save-copy/cancel protection and completed-reference reload. Final browser scripts run serially with isolated profiles and frozen per-viewport HTML after intermittent reload failures were observed with concurrent file browsers. Startup workspace/toast diagnostics are retained on failure; no application persistence change was made.

Final root index.html, dist/index.html, frozen browser inputs and all per-viewport copies match byte for byte. Desktop topologies and light/dark mobile guides were visually reviewed. The complete generated stylesheet is byte-identical to the prior app, and CLI colors are checked in all twelve new-lab viewport cases.
scope: Adds two IPv4 OSPFv2 catalog labs and their guides, completed references, command resources, documentation and validation. Repairs IOS interface-membership removal and extends bounded lesson predicates for configured priority and elected role. Existing packet-driven OSPF and forwarding engines remain unchanged. No theme, terminal styling, backend or dependency changes. No new OSPFv3, NBMA, multi-area or live CML validation claim; no new claim of wire-level Hello election or Wait-timer fidelity beyond the existing election model.
